findings.highlight: I was ready to look down on her and give her a lecture or two.
findings.evidenceJa: 自分のことを棚に上げ、説教の一つでもかますつもりで気合いを入れていた。
findings.explanation: Haruki was steeling himself to lecture Youko while setting aside his own failings—an explicit acknowledgment of hypocrisy. The English instead says he intended to look down on her, replacing self-reproach with contempt for Youko.
findings.japanese:
自分のことを棚に上げ、説教の一つでもかますつもりで
気合いを入れていた。
findings.todokanai: I was ready to look down on her and give her a lecture or two.

findings.highlight: "The fatality rate for this disease has gone down considerably in recent years. And I've been using plenty of both medications and money. I'll make it to a hundred at the very least."
findings.evidenceJa:
「最近はだいぶこの病気の致死率も下がってきてるし、
薬打ちまくって、金使いまくって、
少なくとも１００までは生き延びるわよ？」
findings.explanation: Youko vows that she will use drugs and money in the future, while the English says she has already been using them — Her defiant commitment to aggressive treatment is still intelligible from the surrounding lines.
findings.japanese:
「最近はだいぶこの病気の致死率も下がってきてるし、
薬打ちまくって、金使いまくって、
少なくとも１００までは生き延びるわよ？」
findings.todokanai: "The fatality rate for this disease has gone down considerably in recent years. And I've been using plenty of both medications and money. I'll make it to a hundred at the very least."

findings.highlight: During our commemorations… or even whenever I feel like it, I can call Kazusa to join our gatherings.
findings.evidenceJa:
お互いや、仲間たちの記念日に…
それどころか、単に思い立っただけでも、
すぐに集まれるメンバーの中にかずさがいる。
findings.explanation: Haruki imagines Kazusa among friends who can gather for one another's anniversaries or on a whim; the English makes Haruki the person who calls her to 'our gatherings.' — The essential fantasy of Kazusa becoming readily present in the old social circle remains.
findings.japanese:
お互いや、仲間たちの記念日に…
それどころか、単に思い立っただけでも、
すぐに集まれるメンバーの中にかずさがいる。
findings.todokanai: During our commemorations… or even whenever I feel like it, I can call Kazusa to join our gatherings.

findings.highlight: It really is… a mockery of art.
findings.evidenceJa: やっぱり芸術って………馬鹿みたいだ。
findings.explanation: Haruki concludes that art itself is absurd or stupid: Kazusa's narrow, childish fixation is precisely what made her art shine. 'A mockery of art' instead implies a debasement of art, reversing the object and direction of his judgment.
findings.japanese: やっぱり芸術って………馬鹿みたいだ。
findings.todokanai: It really is… a mockery of art.

findings.highlight: Being with someone so troublesome is impossible for you, just as I suspected.
findings.evidenceJa: 「だってギター君、普通の人だもの。そんなハードルの高い相手、やっぱりあの子には無理だったのよ」
findings.explanation: Youko says that an ordinary man is too high a hurdle for Kazusa: Kazusa cannot live normally without destroying the world around him. The English reverses the relationship, calling Kazusa troublesome and saying she is impossible for Haruki.
findings.japanese:
「だってギター君、普通の人だもの。
そんなハードルの高い相手、
やっぱりあの子には無理だったのよ」
findings.todokanai: "Because you're an ordinary person, Guitar-kun. Being with someone so troublesome is impossible for you, just as I suspected."

findings.highlight: To other people, that would be a very brutal, heartless and terrible thing.
findings.evidenceJa: 「それは、別のある人にとっては、とても残酷で、無情で、本当に酷いこと」
findings.explanation: Youko refers to one particular other person—Setsuna—for whom Kazusa taking Haruki would be cruel. The English pluralizes her into generic 'other people,' erasing the pointed third member of the triangle.
findings.japanese:
「それは、別のある人にとっては、
とても残酷で、無情で、本当に酷いこと」
findings.todokanai: "To other people, that would be a very brutal, heartless and terrible thing."

findings.highlight: what about the people who were around me when I lived an ordinary life…?
findings.evidenceJa: そして、もしリスクを覚悟で飛び込んだとしても、その時、普通の俺の側にいようとしてくれていた人は…
findings.explanation: Haruki thinks of the single person who had been trying to stay by ordinary Haruki's side—Setsuna. The English turns her into plural people who merely happened to be around him, losing both the referent and her sustained effort.
findings.japanese:
そして、もしリスクを覚悟で飛び込んだとしても、
その時、普通の俺の側にいようとしてくれていた人は…
findings.todokanai: Even if I jumped into it with full awareness of the risks, what about the people who were around me when I lived an ordinary life…?

findings.highlight: So make sure you don't forget that.
findings.evidenceJa: 「だから、これからも忘れない。下手をしたら…いえ、今のままじゃ確実に、一生、新しい恋なんてできるわけがない」
findings.explanation: Youko says Kazusa will continue not to forget Haruki and, at this rate, will certainly never love anyone new. The English changes the first sentence into an instruction for Haruki to remember Youko's warning.
findings.japanese:
「だから、これからも忘れない。
下手をしたら…いえ、今のままじゃ確実に、
一生、新しい恋なんてできるわけがない」
findings.todokanai: "So make sure you don't forget that. If she's unlucky… No, it's almost certain that she'll never fall in love again her whole life at this rate."

findings.highlight: I can manage to stay in Setsuna's room overnight all the time.
findings.evidenceJa: …まぁ、逆にこういう一家だからこそ、雪菜を大っぴらに部屋に泊めることもできるんだけど。
findings.explanation: Haruki says this family's openness is what lets him openly have Setsuna stay overnight in his room. The English reverses both the guest and the room, saying Haruki repeatedly stays in Setsuna's room.
findings.japanese:
…まぁ、逆にこういう一家だからこそ、
雪菜を大っぴらに部屋に泊めることもできるんだけど。
findings.todokanai: …Well, on the other hand, it's precisely because this family is the way it is that I can manage to stay in Setsuna's room overnight all the time.

findings.evidenceJa: この、軽くて浮き足立った雰囲気の中でも。一世一代の決め所かもしれなかった場面でも…
findings.explanation: The family is in a light, excited, almost giddy mood as they anticipate a marriage. Calling the atmosphere 'heavy' reverses the contrast: Haruki is sinking internally despite everyone else's buoyancy.
findings.japanese:
この、軽くて浮き足立った雰囲気の中でも。
一世一代の決め所かもしれなかった場面でも…
findings.todokanai: Amidst this heavy atmosphere, and in this place where my once in a lifetime choice could be made…

findings.highlight: In fact, it was probably the best way to go about it.
findings.evidenceJa: 気が早すぎても、問題ないはずだった。それどころか、正式に申し込むべき話の流れだった。
findings.explanation: Haruki says that, far from the family merely being premature, the conversation had reached the point where he should formally propose/ask for Setsuna's hand. The English reduces this decisive missed act to a vague 'best way to go about it.'
findings.japanese:
気が早すぎても、問題ないはずだった。
それどころか、正式に申し込むべき話の流れだった。
findings.todokanai: There shouldn't be anything wrong with being eager. In fact, it was probably the best way to go about it.

findings.highlight: Setsuna's mother started talking about the future of the household, putting her in direct opposition to the children who insisted on talking about that with only the family around.
findings.evidenceJa: お母さんは、もう親戚の予定を気にしだして、『内輪で』を多用する若手組と真っ向から対立し。
findings.explanation: Setsuna's mother is already worrying about relatives' schedules, while the younger group repeatedly insists on keeping the wedding intimate or within the family. The English invents a discussion about the household's future and mistakes 内輪で for privately discussing it with family present.
findings.japanese:
お母さんは、もう親戚の予定を気にしだして、
『内輪で』を多用する若手組と真っ向から対立し。
findings.todokanai: Setsuna's mother started talking about the future of the household, putting her in direct opposition to the children who insisted on talking about that with only the family around.

findings.highlight: I feel like I'm at the edge of a violent passion. One that is trying to make me forget about everything…
findings.evidenceJa: まるで何もかも忘れようとしているかのような、激しい情欲のぶつけあいの果てに…
findings.explanation: Haruki is looking back on what came at the end of their violent mutual collision of lust, as if both were trying to forget everything. The English turns the aftermath into a present feeling 'at the edge' of an abstract passion and loses the mutual sexual act.
findings.japanese:
まるで何もかも忘れようとしているかのような、
激しい情欲のぶつけあいの果てに…
findings.todokanai: I feel like I'm at the edge of a violent passion. One that is trying to make me forget about everything…
